subproblems.title: Operator vs Hilbert–Schmidt norm, distance to a subspace, and the projection trace identity
subproblems.statement:
(i) For all m, k and every linear map A : R^m → R^k, ‖A‖ <= |A|, where ‖A‖ is the operator norm and |A| = (Σ_i |A e_i|^2)^{1/2} = hsNorm A is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (e_i the standard basis).
(ii) For every linear subspace T ⊆ R^m and v ∈ R^m, |p_{T⊥} v| = dist(v, T), where p_{T⊥} is the orthogonal projection onto T⊥.
(iii) For linear subspaces P, T ⊆ R^m with dim P = dim T, trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p_P) = (1/2)|p_P − p_T|^2, where |·|^2 = hsNormSq.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (m k : ℕ) (A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), ‖A‖ ≤ hsNorm A) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)) (v : Rn m), ‖Tᗮ.starProjection v‖ = Metric.infDist v (T : Set (Rn m))) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (P T : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)), Module.finrank ℝ P = Module.finrank ℝ T → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn m) (Tᗮ.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = hsNormSq (P.starProjection - T.starProjection) / 2

Context. This child supplies part (i), ||A|| <= hsNorm A, to gwe_gta_proj_inner_defect (Simon 4.5 (10)-(11)), where it is applied at that child's arbitrary m with k = m, and part (iii), trace(p_{T-perp} o p_P) = hsNormSq(p_P - p_T)/2 when dim P = dim T, to gwe_gta_vertical_trace_sum (Simon 4.4), where it is applied with m = n + l (Amb n l is by definition Rn (n + l)). Part (ii) is not used here. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.projection_algebra-a1 (candidate commit 164f08e), reused with its identical frozen Lean type, title, statement and dependency list; the proof below is the accepted argument formalized there. Inside that proof, 'the parent proof', 'the supplied proof' and 'Source' refer to the original parent of that DAG node, and 'sibling' to its original siblings, whose keys coincide with the keys used here.

Source: the supplied proof's facts
- (F3) (Simon 5.2.1 proof, display (2));
- '||A|| <= |A|' (step 5);
- '|x'| = dist(x − ξ, T)' (step 7).

Setting: R^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with orthonormal basis e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, hsNormSq A = Σ_i ‖A e_i‖^2 and hsNorm A = (hsNormSq A)^{1/2}. Every subspace W of R^m is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so the orthogonal projection p_W := W.starProjection exists. It is self-adjoint and idempotent, with range W and kernel W⊥.

(i) Operator norm <= Hilbert–Schmidt norm.
1. Let v ∈ R^m have coordinates v_i. Then v = Σ_i v_i e_i and ‖v‖^2 = Σ_i v_i^2.
2. By linearity, A v = Σ_i v_i A e_i. The triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz in R^m give
    ‖A v‖ <= Σ_i |v_i| ‖A e_i‖ <= (Σ_i v_i^2)^{1/2} (Σ_i ‖A e_i‖^2)^{1/2} = ‖v‖ · hsNorm A.
3. hsNorm A >= 0, so the operator-norm bound (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound) gives ‖A‖ <= hsNorm A.

(ii) Distance to a subspace.
4. v = p_T v + p_{T⊥} v (Submodule.starProjection_add_starProjection_orthogonal). So ‖p_{T⊥} v‖ = ‖v − p_T v‖ = dist(v, p_T v).
5. Let w ∈ T. Then v − w = (v − p_T v) + (p_T v − w), with v − p_T v ∈ T⊥ and p_T v − w ∈ T. By Pythagoras,
    ‖v − w‖^2 = ‖v − p_T v‖^2 + ‖p_T v − w‖^2 >= ‖v − p_T v‖^2,
  with equality at w = p_T v ∈ T. Hence infDist(v, T) = inf_{w ∈ T} ‖v − w‖ = ‖v − p_T v‖ (Mathlib Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give ‖p_{T⊥} v‖ = infDist(v, T). This is exactly SimonGMT Chapter04.norm_normalProjection_eq_infDist.

(iii) The trace identity.
7. Write p := p_P, q := p_T and k := dim P = dim T. An orthogonal projection onto W is a projection onto W along W⊥, so its trace is dim W (LinearMap.IsProj.trace; equivalently, in an orthonormal basis adapted to W ⊕ W⊥ its matrix is diag(1,…,1,0,…,0)). So trace p = trace q = k.
8. By step 4 applied to every vector, p_{T⊥} = I − q. Hence
    trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p) = trace p − trace(q ∘ p) = k − trace(qp).
9. For any linear B on R^m, hsNormSq B = Σ_i ‖B e_i‖^2 = Σ_i ⟨B^*B e_i, e_i⟩ = trace(B^*B). This uses that in an orthonormal basis the trace of C is Σ_i ⟨C e_i, e_i⟩ (the diagonal of its matrix).
10. B := p − q is self-adjoint, and p^2 = p, q^2 = q, so B^*B = (p − q)^2 = p − pq − qp + q. With trace(pq) = trace(qp) (LinearMap.trace_mul_comm),
    hsNormSq(p − q) = trace p + trace q − 2 trace(qp) = 2k − 2 trace(qp).
11. By steps 8 and 10, hsNormSq(p − q)/2 = k − trace(qp) = trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p_P). In Lean form: LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn m) (Tᗮ.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = hsNormSq (P.starProjection − T.starProjection)/2. ∎

subproblems.title: Coordinates, linearity, norm and inner product of graphPoint
subproblems.statement: For all n, l >= 0, let Amb n l = R^(n+l) (EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n + l))) and, for a in R^n and b in R^l, let graphPoint(a, b) := toLp(Fin.append a b) be the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a and whose last l coordinates are those of b. Then: (C1) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and i in Fin n, the coordinate of graphPoint(a, b) at castAdd l i is a_i; (C2) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and j in Fin l, the coordinate of graphPoint(a, b) at natAdd n j is b_j; and for all a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l and t in R: (L1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint(a, b) + graphPoint(a', b'); (L2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a', b'); (L3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint(a, b); (L4) |graphPoint(a, b)|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (IP) <graphPoint(a, b), graphPoint(a', b')> = <a, a'> + <b, b'> (real Euclidean inner products of R^(n+l), R^n and R^l).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ) (i : Fin n), graphPoint a b (Fin.castAdd ℓ i) = a i) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ) (j : Fin ℓ), graphPoint a b (Fin.natAdd n j) = b j) ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a + a') (b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), graphPoint (t • a) (t • b) = t • graphPoint a b) ∧ (∀ (a : Rn n) (b : Rn ℓ), ‖graphPoint a b‖ ^ 2 = ‖a‖ ^ 2 + ‖b‖ ^ 2) ∧ (∀ (a a' : Rn n) (b b' : Rn ℓ), inner ℝ (graphPoint a b) (graphPoint a' b') = inner ℝ a a' + inner ℝ b b')
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This child supplies the graph-point calculus: the coordinates (C1), (C2) and (L3) to gwe_gta_vertical_trace_sum, (L2) and (IP) to gwe_gta_graph_row_orthogonal, and (L4), (IP) to the parent's assembly (|q(graphPoint a 0)| = |a| and <q(graphPoint a 0), q(graphPoint b 0)> = <a, b>). It is also the dependency of the reused sibling rotated_plane. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.allard_any_radius-a1.graph_rate-a1.la_basics-a1.graph_coords-a1 (candidate commit 600de56), reused with its identical frozen Lean type, title, statement and dependency list; the proof below is the accepted argument formalized there. Inside that proof, 'the parent proof', 'the supplied proof' and 'Source' refer to the original parent of that DAG node, and 'sibling' to its original siblings, whose keys coincide with the keys used here.

Notation. N := n + l. For x in R^N = Amb n l and k in Fin N, x_k is the k-th coordinate of x; similarly for vectors of R^n and R^l. By definition graphPoint a b = toLp(Fin.append a b), the vector of R^N whose coordinate function is Fin.append (coordinates of a) (coordinates of b).

1. Index decomposition. Every k in Fin N is of one of the forms castAdd l i with i in Fin n (value i < n) or natAdd n j with j in Fin l (value n + j >= n) (Fin.addCases). The maps castAdd l and natAdd n are injective, and castAdd l i is never equal to natAdd n j, because their values satisfy i < n <= n + j.

2. (C1), (C2). Fin.append evaluates at castAdd l i to the i-th entry of its first argument and at natAdd n j to the j-th entry of its second argument (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right), and the coordinates of toLp f are the values of f. Hence (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i and (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j.

3. Extensionality. Two vectors of R^N are equal if and only if their coordinates agree at every k in Fin N, and by step 1 it suffices to compare them at every castAdd l i (i in Fin n) and at every natAdd n j (j in Fin l). Sums, differences and scalar multiples in R^N, R^n and R^l are computed coordinatewise.

4. (L1). At castAdd l i the left side has coordinate (a + a')_i = a_i + a'_i by (C1), and the right side has coordinate (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} + (graphPoint a' b')_{castAdd l i} = a_i + a'_i by (C1). At natAdd n j both sides have coordinate b_j + b'_j by (C2). By step 3 the two vectors are equal.

5. (L2). Exactly as in step 4 with differences: at castAdd l i both coordinates are a_i - a'_i, and at natAdd n j both are b_j - b'_j, by (C1), (C2).

6. (L3). Exactly as in step 4 with scalar multiples: at castAdd l i both coordinates are t a_i, and at natAdd n j both are t b_j, by (C1), (C2).

7. (L4). In the Euclidean space R^N, |x|^2 = sum_{k in Fin N} x_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq; for reals |x_k|^2 = x_k^2), and likewise |a|^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} a_i^2 in R^n and |b|^2 = sum_{j in Fin l} b_j^2 in R^l. A sum over Fin (n + l) equals the sum over i in Fin n of the term at castAdd l i plus the sum over j in Fin l of the term at natAdd n j (Fin.sum_univ_add, which is the bijection of step 1). Applying this to x = graphPoint a b and using (C1), (C2): |graphPoint a b|^2 = sum_{i} a_i^2 + sum_{j} b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.

8. (IP). The real inner product of R^N is <x, y> = sum_{k in Fin N} x_k y_k (PiLp.inner_apply; for real scalars the summand <x_k, y_k> is the product x_k y_k), and likewise in R^n and R^l. Splitting the sum as in step 7 and using (C1), (C2) for both graphPoint a b and graphPoint a' b': <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = sum_{i} a_i a'_i + sum_{j} b_j b'_j = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

Every step is valid for all n, l >= 0: if n = 0 or l = 0, the corresponding index case of step 1 does not occur and the corresponding sums are empty.
proof_key_steps: Every index of Fin (n+l) is exactly one of castAdd l i or natAdd n j, and Fin.append gives the coordinates a_i and b_j there: (C1), (C2)
(L1)-(L3) by comparing coordinates at both kinds of indices (extensionality in R^(n+l))
(L4) and (IP) by splitting the coordinate sums |x|^2 = sum_k x_k^2 and <x,y> = sum_k x_k y_k with Fin.sum_univ_add and applying (C1), (C2)

subproblems.title: Projection onto, distance to, and dimension of the rotated plane T_0 = q(R^n x {0})
subproblems.statement: For all n, l >= 0 and every linear isometric equivalence q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l onto itself: let graphPoint(a, b) be the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l, horizontalPlane := span{eps_{castAdd l i} : i in Fin n} (eps_k the standard basis vectors of R^(n+l)), T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane) (the image of horizontalPlane under the linear map underlying q) and P_{T_0} := (rotatedPlane q).starProjection its orthogonal projection. Then (L5) P_{T_0}(q(graphPoint(a, b))) = q(graphPoint(a, 0)) for all a in R^n, b in R^l; (L6) infDist(q(graphPoint(a, b)), T_0) = |b| for all a in R^n, b in R^l; (L7) finrank T_0 = n.

Context. This child supplies (L5), P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0) for P the orthogonal projection onto T = rotatedPlane q, and (L7), finrank T = n, to gwe_gta_vertical_trace_sum, and (L5) to the parent's assembly (q(graphPoint a 0) lies in T). (L6) is not used here. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.allard_any_radius-a1.graph_rate-a1.la_basics-a1.rotated_plane-a1 (candidate commit b1a6014), reused with its identical frozen Lean type, title, statement and dependency list (here expressed through the sibling key(s) graph_coords); the proof below is the accepted argument formalized there. Inside that proof, 'the parent proof', 'the supplied proof' and 'Source' refer to the original parent of that DAG node, and 'sibling' to its original siblings, whose keys coincide with the keys used here.

Notation. N := n + l; eps_k (k in Fin N) are the standard basis vectors of R^N = Amb n l and e_i (i in Fin n) those of R^n. horizontalPlane = span{eps_{castAdd l i} : i in Fin n}, and T_0 = rotatedPlane q = {q(h) : h in horizontalPlane}. From the sibling theorem graph_coords (Submission.any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra) at n, l we use: (C1) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and i in Fin n, (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i; (C2) for all a in R^n, b in R^l and j in Fin l, (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j; and for all a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l and t in R: (L1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint a b + graphPoint a' b'; (L2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b'; (L3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint a b; (L4) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (IP) <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

1. eps_{castAdd l i} = graphPoint(e_i, 0) for every i in Fin n. Compare coordinates; every index of Fin N is castAdd l i' (i' in Fin n) or natAdd n j (j in Fin l) (Fin.addCases). At castAdd l i' the left side is 1 if castAdd l i' = castAdd l i, i.e. i' = i (castAdd l is injective, Fin.castAdd_injective), and 0 otherwise; the right side is (e_i)_{i'} by (C1), which is also 1 if i' = i and 0 otherwise. At natAdd n j the left side is 0, because natAdd n j is not castAdd l i (their values satisfy n + j >= n > i); the right side is the j-th coordinate of 0 in R^l, i.e. 0, by (C2).

2. The map G : R^n -> R^N, G(c) := graphPoint(c, 0), is linear: G(c + c') = graphPoint(c + c', 0 + 0) = G(c) + G(c') by (L1), and G(t c) = graphPoint(t c, t 0) = t G(c) by (L3), using 0 + 0 = 0 and t 0 = 0 in R^l.

3. horizontalPlane = {graphPoint(c, 0) : c in R^n}.
(a) For c in R^n write c = sum_i c_i e_i. By step 2 and step 1, graphPoint(c, 0) = G(c) = sum_i c_i G(e_i) = sum_i c_i eps_{castAdd l i}, a linear combination of the spanning vectors; hence graphPoint(c, 0) lies in horizontalPlane.

subproblems.title: Graph orthogonality: p_S e'_j = p_S q(r, 0) when r is the j-th row of D (Simon 4.5 (7))
subproblems.statement: For all n, l in N, every linear isometry equivalence q of R^(n+l), every continuous linear map D : R^n -> R^l, every j in Fin l and every r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v in R^n: let S := span_R{q(graphPoint v (D v)) : v in R^n} and p := S.starProjection. Then p(q(graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))) = p(q(graphPoint r 0)). Here graphPoint a b is the point of R^(n+l) whose first n coordinates are those of a in R^n and whose last l coordinates are those of b in R^l.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (j : Fin ℓ) (r : Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, inner ℝ r v = D v j) → (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) = (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (D v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint r 0))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is Simon 4.5 (7) ('e_{n+j} - (grad f^j, 0) is normal to the graph'), step 4 of the parent proof. The parent applies it with D = Df(x') and r the j-th row of D. Prerequisite: graph_coords (GA, Submission.any_radius_gr_la_graphPoint_algebra): (L2) graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') = graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b'; (IP) <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

Notation. Fix n, l, q, D, j and r with <r, v> = (D v)_j for every v in R^n. d_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 in R^l, e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 d_j), g := q(graphPoint r 0), S := span_R{q(graphPoint v (D v)) : v in R^n} and p := S.starProjection (it exists since R^{n+l} is finite-dimensional).

1. The difference. Put x := e'_j - g. Since q is linear, x = q(graphPoint 0 d_j - graphPoint r 0), and by (L2) (read from right to left with a = 0, a' = r, b = d_j, b' = 0), graphPoint 0 d_j - graphPoint r 0 = graphPoint (0 - r) (d_j - 0). So x = q(graphPoint (0 - r) (d_j - 0)) = q(graphPoint (-r) d_j).
2. x is orthogonal to every generator of S. Let v be in R^n. The linear isometry equivalence q preserves inner products (LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_map), so by (IP)
 <x, q(graphPoint v (D v))> = <graphPoint (-r) d_j, graphPoint v (D v)> = <-r, v> + <d_j, D v>.
 Here <-r, v> = -<r, v> = -(D v)_j by the hypothesis on r, and <d_j, y> = y_j for every y in R^l (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left with the scalar 1). Hence <x, q(graphPoint v (D v))> = -(D v)_j + (D v)_j = 0.
3. x lies in S-perp. The set of vectors y with <x, y> = 0 is the subspace (R x)-perp (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right). By step 2 it contains every generator q(graphPoint v (D v)), so it contains their span S (Submodule.span_le). Thus <x, y> = 0 for every y in S, i.e. x lies in S-perp (Submodule.mem_orthogonal').
4. Conclusion. The orthogonal projection onto S vanishes exactly on S-perp (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff), so p x = 0. By linearity, 0 = p x = p e'_j - p g, i.e. p(q(graphPoint 0 d_j)) = p(q(graphPoint r 0)). QED

subproblems.title: Rows of a linear map: |r| <= ||D|| for every row r, and a row family with sum_j |R_j|^2 = |D|^2
subproblems.statement: For all n, l in N and every continuous linear map D : R^n -> R^l: (i) for every j in Fin l and every r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v in R^n, |r| <= ||D|| (operator norm); (ii) there is a family (R_j)_{j in Fin l} in R^n with <R_j, v> = (D v)_j for all j in Fin l and v in R^n, and sum_{j in Fin l} |R_j|^2 = hsNormSq D = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2 (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), (∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (r : Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, inner ℝ r v = D v j) → ‖r‖ ≤ ‖D‖) ∧ ∃ R : Fin ℓ → Rn n, (∀ (j : Fin ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (R j) v = D v j) ∧ ∑ j : Fin ℓ, ‖R j‖ ^ 2 = hsNormSq D
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is step 3 of the parent proof (rows of D = Df(x'), i.e. the gradients grad f^j). The parent uses (i) to get |r| <= ||D|| <= 1 and (ii) to write |D|^2 = sum_j |r_j|^2. No sibling prerequisites; only Mathlib facts about EuclideanSpace are used.

Notation. Fix n, l and D : R^n -> R^l continuous linear. e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n (i in Fin n); y_j is the j-th coordinate of y in R^l; <.,.> and |.| are the Euclidean inner product and norm; ||D|| is the operator norm; hsNormSq D = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2.

(i) Row norm bound.
1. Let j in Fin l and r in R^n with <r, v> = (D v)_j for all v. Taking v = r:
 |r|^2 = <r, r> = (D r)_j <= |(D r)_j| <= |D r| <= ||D|| |r|.
 Here |y_j| <= |y| for every y in R^l (PiLp.norm_apply_le) and |D r| <= ||D|| |r| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
2. If |r| = 0, then |r| = 0 <= ||D|| because operator norms are nonnegative. If |r| > 0, dividing |r|^2 <= ||D|| |r| by |r| gives |r| <= ||D||.

(ii) Rows with sum of squares |D|^2.
3. Construction. For j in Fin l, the map v |-> (D v)_j is a continuous linear functional on R^n: the composite (EuclideanSpace.proj j) o D. By the Riesz representation theorem in the finite-dimensional inner product space R^n, R_j := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (Rn n)).symm ((EuclideanSpace.proj j) o D) satisfies <R_j, v> = (D v)_j for every v (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply). (Equivalently R_j is the vector with coordinates (R_j)_i = (D e_i)_j, and <R_j, v> = sum_i (D e_i)_j v_i = (D (sum_i v_i e_i))_j = (D v)_j.)
4. Coordinates. For every i in Fin n, (R_j)_i = <R_j, e_i> (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right with the scalar 1) = (D e_i)_j by step 3.
5. Parseval. In a Euclidean space |x|^2 is the sum of the squares of the coordinates (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). Hence, by step 4,
 sum_{j in Fin l} |R_j|^2 = sum_{j in Fin l} sum_{i in Fin n} (D e_i)_j^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} sum_{j in Fin l} (D e_i)_j^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} |D e_i|^2 = hsNormSq D,
 where the middle equality exchanges two finite sums (Finset.sum_comm) and the third applies Parseval in R^l to each D e_i.
6. Steps 3 and 5 give the family R = (R_j)_j required in (ii). For l = 0 or n = 0 the sums are empty and both sides are 0. QED
